title: Reconsidering AI w / Steve Klabnik
summary: Steve Klabnik on how to have productive conversations about AI, plus his own shift from AI skeptic to agentic-coding user once models improved.

assertions.quote: I think that the new models really went from like not being useful to being useful for me
I hated spicy autocomplete and I love agentic style coding
being forced by management to adopt these tools. And that caused a lot of heat and a lot of argument
everyone was talking about prompt engineering a year ago, but like now it's about context engineering
it is also true there's a learning curve

verdicts.note: Gains appeared on first use: in the follow-up, after removing participants with prior GenAI coding experience, the main quantity and quality effects still held (brief, simple tasks).

assertions.quote: getting my fingers into the details is like not as interesting to me as it was before

verdicts.note: A plausible point about personal preference that has not been systematically measured.

Anthropic interviews (53): engineers who 'enjoy what I get out of writing code' or think at the product level embrace Claude, while those who value flow-state hands-on coding mourn it; whether people embrace it 'depends on what aspects of software engineering they find most meaningful' (qualitative, not about reviewing per se).
